diagram_math_checks.check: Definition lines 39 and 53 give input (V,(x_j)_{j in V}), with x_j in R^q, and output (z_j)_{j in V} in Z^V. The first arrow is labelled encoder without borrowing the unmasked E_phi:X->Z interface. Only visible patches and their positions enter it; no mask token does.

Definition lines 39 and 53 specify one learned m in Z reused at every missing position. For explanatory abbreviation t_j, the figure sets t_j=z_j for j in V and t_j=m for j not in V; hence (t_1,...,t_M) is in Z^M. All M slot positions accompany this sequence. This is slot assembly, not a learned projection.
Definition line 53 gives predictions hat x_j(phi,psi;x,V) in R^q for every j in [M]. The decoder arrow therefore ends at (hat x_j)_{j=1}^M in (R^q)^M, not merely at masked-patch predictions.

The last box repeats line 61 with sum over [M] minus V and denominator (M-k)q. There are M-k masked patches, each having q real coordinates; k<M makes the denominator positive. Both hat x_j and T(x_j) lie in R^q; caption preserves the positive-standard-deviation restriction for normalized targets from lines 55-60. No full-image-risk identity or unbiasedness is drawn.

The four downward arrows express the sequential data processing and loss evaluation already specified in Definition, not commutative equalities. Parameters phi,psi and fixed x,V,T are suppressed only in the diagram abbreviations. The complete original Definition and references remain byte-identical; no rigorous proof depends on the figure.
